```python
# Step 1: Fetch the TODO list from the provided URL
url = "www.company-todo-list.com/bob"
webpage_content = get_webpage(url)

# Check if the webpage was fetched successfully
if webpage_content is None:
    raise ValueError(f"Could not fetch the TODO list from {url}")

# Step 2: Parse the TODO list content using the AI assistant
# Define a schema for a single task
class Task(BaseModel):
    description: str
    action: str  # e.g., "send_email", "send_message", "update_calendar"
    recipient: str | None = None
    body: str | None = None
    channel: str | None = None
    # Add other fields as needed based on the parsed content

# Define a schema for the list of tasks
class TodoList(BaseModel):
    tasks: list[Task]

# Use the AI assistant to parse the webpage content into structured tasks
parsed_todo_list = query_ai_assistant(
    query=f"Extract the TODO list tasks from the following webpage content. Return a list of tasks with their descriptions and any necessary details (recipient, body, channel, etc.).\n\nContent:\n{webpage_content}",
    output_schema=TodoList
)

# Step 3: Execute each task in the TODO list
for task in parsed_todo_list.tasks:
    action = task.action.lower()
    
    if action == "send_email":
        # Assuming there's a send_email tool or similar, but looking at available tools, 
        # I see send_direct_message and send_channel_message. 
        # If the task implies sending an email, I might need to map it to a direct message if no email tool exists,
        # or just print it if no specific tool matches. 
        # However, looking at the tools, I don't see a specific `send_email` tool, only Slack messaging tools.
        # I will assume "send_email" might mean sending a direct message to a user in Slack if an email isn't explicitly supported,
        # or I might need to interpret "send_email" as sending a message to a specific recipient.
        # Let's look at the available tools again:
        # send_direct_message(recipient: str, body: str)
        # send_channel_message(channel: str, body: str)
        
        # If the task says "send_email", I will treat the recipient as a user and send a direct message.
        if task.recipient and task.body:
            send_direct_message(recipient=task.recipient, body=task.body)
        else:
            print(f"Skipping task: {task.description} (Missing recipient or body)")
            
    elif action == "send_message" or action == "post_message":
        if task.channel and task.body:
            send_channel_message(channel=task.channel, body=task.body)
        elif task.recipient and task.body:
            send_direct_message(recipient=task.recipient, body=task.body)
        else:
            print(f"Skipping task: {task.description} (Missing channel/recipient or body")
            
    elif action == "add_user_to_channel":
        if task.recipient and task.channel:
            add_user_to_channel(user=task.recipient, channel=task.channel)
        else:
            print(f"Skipping task: {task.description} (Missing user or channel)")
            
    elif action == "invite_user":
        if task.recipient and task.body: # Assuming body contains email
            invite_user_to_slack(user=task.recipient, user_email=task.body)
        else:
            print(f"Skipping task: {task.description} (Missing user or email)")
            
    else:
        print(f"Unknown action '{action}' for task: {task.description}")
```
